requirements.evidence: All five routes with correct names/middleware (routes/web.php:13-31: guest group, 'throttle:6,1' on password.email, verification.verify with ['auth','signed','throttle:6,1']); store always returns back()->with('status', __('passwords.sent')) (PasswordResetController.php:42); update validates PasswordRule::min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() + confirmed, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset, redirects to '/' (lines 61-87); VerifyEmailController aborts 403 on id/hash mismatch and redirects '/' (lines 18-33); phpunit.xml pins APP_NAME/APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE; .env.example updated; mail.markdown.theme='pegafila' and theme uses #0f7490 on .button-primary; pt_BR.json adds 'Reset your password' and 'Verify your email address'. Not verifiable from the diff that the body/sub-copy strings of the installed Laravel version are all present in pt_BR.json, and nothing (no test) demonstrates the rendered mail is translated.

conventions.evidence: Conventions require test-first and 'everything implemented ships with a test' — the diff has no test files at all. No CHANGELOG.md/docs update. PasswordResetController::update validates four fields inline (lines 61-70) where conventions call for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields. Views are bare unstyled forms without Bulma (acceptable given layouts are out of scope). PHPDoc present on public methods.

security.evidence: Inputs validated server-side; Blade uses {{ }} escaping and @csrf; guest middleware and throttle on reset request; hash_equals used for id/hash in VerifyEmailController.php:18-24; forceFill limited to password/remember_token. Minor: store() does its own User::where lookup before sendResetLink (line 35-39), adding a timing difference between existing and non-existing addresses; password.update has no throttle (token-protected, low impact).

tests.evidence: No Pest/PHPUnit test files in the diff: nothing covers the translated mail rendering, theme color, the 'never reveal existence' behaviour, password rule validation, token rotation, or the 403 paths of verification.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean and uses framework facilities (Password::sendResetLink, Password::reset, PasswordRule). Redundant pre-lookup `User::where('email', ...)->first()` (PasswordResetController.php:35) duplicates what sendResetLink already does; view fallbacks `$token ?? request()->route('token')` and `$email ?? request()->query('email')` (reset-password.blade.php:3,5) duplicate what the controller passes. Theme CSS is a full copy of Laravel's default theme, which is how custom themes work.

readability.evidence: Clear method names (create/store/edit/update), short methods, PHPDoc comments, consistent with Laravel starter-kit style; no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Changes serve the task. Small extra: User now implements MustVerifyEmail (app/Models/User.php:15), which is not required by the task (hasVerifiedEmail/markEmailAsVerified are available via the base Authenticatable trait) and changes registration behaviour for the separate auth task. config/mail.php also adds a 'paths' entry beyond the theme.

issues.explanation: The change ships no tests at all, violating the project's mandatory test-first rule and leaving every requirement (translated mails, theme, non-disclosure, validation, verification 403s) unverified.
Only the two subject keys were added; nothing in the diff confirms the body and sub-copy strings of the installed Laravel version are translated, and no test renders the mail to prove it.
Four-field validation is inline instead of a Form Request, contrary to the project's validation convention.
No CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry or docs update for the new routes and mail theme.
The redundant manual user lookup before sendResetLink adds a timing difference between existing and unknown addresses; Password::sendResetLink already handles unknown users.
Making User implement MustVerifyEmail is not required and alters registration/verification behaviour owned by another task.
Fallbacks to request()->route('token') and request()->query('email') duplicate values the controller already passes.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR locale pins, the pegafila mail theme with #0f7490 on the button, the subject translations, the password-reset routes/controller and the verification endpoint, largely matching the contract. However it ships with no tests whatsoever, which the project's conventions make mandatory, and skips docs/CHANGELOG and the Form Request convention, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
